decisions.reason: Cites LinkType Junction + Target and the cordis.patch.yml link: marker to establish two names for one tree; edits are already deployed; copy is a no-op and harmful; distinguishes blank-LinkType copied installs.

Host process owns both open file handles and boot-cached module/bundle state; closing a tab removes the consumer not the lock owner; browser HTTP cache is treated as a separate second layer needing hard refresh after restart, with no over-generalization.

Explains the rename hit the unique physical file so the follow-up source copy failed; renames .old2 back preserving contents, node --checks both, then activates; host stop treated as valid precaution, no file recreation required.
Order: edit, node --check, fully stop host, restart dsh web, hard-refresh bypassing browser cache, then verify marker/body, UI behavior, new host route, and absence of boot errors.

Pre-flight probes (LinkType/Target, link: marker, package.json link dependency) before any file operation, branching linked vs copied procedure, and a clear explanation of how generic copy advice caused the data-loss incident.

caps.reason: Final plan contains no copy step and forbids deleting .old2 before verified restore; copy-through-junction appears only as rejected/quoted bad advice.
Plan mandates full host stop and restart; refresh-not-a-host-stop appears only as a refuted misconception.
